title: HB 560 (2019-2020 (133th General Assembly)): H. B. No. 560: Modify the law governing elections
operative_text:
(a_in_person_id)
(section) 3505.18(A)(1)
(quote) to cast ballots in person at a precinct polling place, a voter service and polling center, or the office of the board of elections, the elector shall announce to the election officials the elector's full name and current address and provide proof of the elector's identity in the form of a current and valid photo identification
(section) 3501.01(AA)(1)
(quote) (1) It shows the name of the individual to whom it was issued, which shall conform to the name in the individual's voter registration record.
(b_no_id_remedy)
(section) 3505.18(A)(2)
(quote) the elector may vote and return mail ballots sent to the elector under section 3509.01 of the Revised Code, request mail ballots at a voter service and polling center or the office of the board, or cast a provisional ballot under section 3505.181 of the Revised Code at any location where ballots may be cast in person.
(section) 3505.18(A)(2)
(quote) STRUCK: (b) Appear at the office of the board of elections not later than the seventh day after the day of the election and provide the identification required under division (A)(1) of this section, the elector's driver's license or state identification card number, or the last four digits of the elector's social security number
(section) 3505.181(B)(7)
(quote) STRUCK: (i) Provide to the board of elections proof of the individual's identity in the form of a current and valid photo identification, a military identification, or a copy of a current utility bill, bank statement, government check, paycheck, or other government document, other than a notice of voter registration mailed by a board of elections under section 3503.19 of the Revised Code, that shows the individual's name and current address; or
(c_mail_ballot_id)
(section) 3509.03(B)(5)
(quote) STRUCK: (5) One of the following: (a) The elector's driver's license number; (b) The last four digits of the elector's social security number; (c) A copy of the elector's current and valid photo identification, a copy of a military identification, or a copy of a current utility bill, bank statement, government check, paycheck, or other government document, other than a notice of voter registration mailed by a board of elections under section 3503.19 of the Revised Code, that shows the name and address of the elector.
(section) 3509.05(A)
(quote) STRUCK: If the elector does not provide the elector's driver's license number or the last four digits of the elector's social security number on the statement of voter on the identification envelope, the elector also shall include in the return envelope with the identification envelope a copy of the elector's current valid photo identification, a copy of a military identification, or a copy of a current utility bill, bank statement, government check, paycheck, or other government document
(d_proof_of_citizenship)
(section) 3505.20
(quote) STRUCK: (4) What official documentation do you possess to prove your citizenship? Please provide that documentation.
(section) 3503.15(H)(1)
(quote) (H) The secretary of state shall conduct an annual review of the statewide voter registration database as follows: (1) The secretary of state shall compare the information in the statewide voter registration database with the information the secretary of state obtains from the bureau of motor vehicles under division (A)(2) of this section to identify any person who does all of the following, in the following order: (a) Submits documentation to the bureau of motor vehicles that indicates that the person is not a United States citizen;
(section) 3503.15(H)(2)
(quote) (2) The secretary of state shall send a written notice to each person identified under division (H)(1) of this section, instructing the person either to confirm that the person is a United States citizen or to submit a completed voter registration cancellation form to the secretary of state.
(e_other_rule) not stated.
(other) 3509.x, 3511.x: absentee voting renamed 'mail ballots'; an elector may apply for mail ballots only in listed cases (3509.03(A)); other electors are sent mail ballots; applications are delivered to the board or a voter service and polling center
(other) 3501.x, 3503.x, 3505.x: 'voter service and polling centers' and 'ballot drop boxes' added across election-administration sections (3501.05, 3503.15(G), 3509.051 and others)
(other) 3503.14: registration form adds optional telephone and e-mail and a list of recognized political parties to choose an affiliation; ends the rule limiting who may sign as the registering person
(other) 3505.18(A)(3)-(5): voter signs the poll book (not writes name and address); a voter who returns mail ballots at a polling place has them kept apart (3505.18(B))
(other) 3505.181: provisional-ballot cure window changes from seven to ten days and applies only to a person successfully challenged under 3505.20
(other) 3505.20: citizenship challenge questions cut to 'Are you a citizen of the United States?'; other questions and the naturalization-certificate proof are struck
(other) 3503.15(H): annual database check against bureau of motor vehicles records of non-citizens (reprinted; only the words 'or change of political party affiliation' are new)
(other) Many other sections (3513.x primaries, 3517.x, 3599.x penalties, 111.26, 124.57, 149.43, 718.01, 4507.06 and others): omnibus election law changes read from the title only
(other) note: Only one version (introduced), with markers; a very large omnibus bill. The in-person ID rule is kept (with new 'cast ballots in person' wording) and absentee/mail-ballot ID is struck, so mail ballots need no ID. The 3503.15(H) citizenship review is existing law reprinted with only a small new phrase; it checks bureau of motor vehicles records of people who showed non-citizen documents and then registered or voted, and only flagged people must confirm citizenship or cancel. Quotes labelled STRUCK are words the bill removes.
